[tool_result: 1	# Bramble Sensor Wire Protocol (BSWP/2.0) — Glasshouse Instruments Consortium, Technical Note TN-0044 (2020)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	BSWP is a compact, half-duplex message protocol for battery-powered environmental sensors
6	deployed inside commercial glasshouses. It targets nodes with 32 KB of flash and no real-time
7	clock, connected over a shared two-wire bus of up to 400 m with as many as 96 nodes per segment.
8	
9	BSWP/2.0 supersedes 1.3. The framing is deliberately unchanged so that a 1.3 gateway can pass
10	2.0 traffic through without understanding it; the payload registers are renumbered and are not
11	compatible.
12	
13	Out of scope: over-the-air firmware delivery (see TN-0051), irrigation valve actuation, and any
14	form of encryption. BSWP assumes a physically trusted bus.
15	
16	## 2. Framing
17	
18	Every frame is a byte sequence:
19	
20	```
21	+------+------+------+--------+-----------+--------+------+
22	| 0xB5 | LEN  | ADDR | OPCODE | PAYLOAD   | CRC16  | 0x5B |
23	+------+------+------+--------+-----------+--------+------+
24	   1      1      1       1       0..247       2       1
25	```
26	
27	- `0xB5` start delimiter, `0x5B` end delimiter.
28	- `LEN` counts `ADDR` through `PAYLOAD` inclusive, so `LEN` ranges 3..250.
29	- `ADDR` is the node address, 0x01–0x60. `0x00` is the gateway. `0xFF` is broadcast.
30	- `CRC16` is CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE over `LEN` through `PAYLOAD`, transmitted big-endian.
31	- Byte stuffing: any `0xB5` or `0x5B` appearing inside `LEN..CRC16` is escaped as `0x7D` followed
32	  by the byte XOR `0x20`. `0x7D` itself is escaped the same way.
33	
34	Maximum on-wire frame length after stuffing is 508 bytes. A receiver that has consumed 508 bytes
35	without seeing `0x5B` discards and resynchronizes on the next `0xB5`.
36	
37	Bus rate is 19200 baud, 8N1. Inter-frame gap is a minimum of 3 character times (1.56 ms).
38	
39	## 3. Addressing and discovery
40	
41	Nodes ship with `ADDR = 0x00` (unconfigured) and a 6-byte factory serial. On power-up an
42	unconfigured node listens only; it never transmits unbidden.
43	
44	The gateway discovers nodes with a binary-search sweep over the serial space:
45	
46	1. Gateway broadcasts `OP_PROBE` (0x11) with a 6-byte prefix and a prefix length in bits.
47	2. Every unconfigured node whose serial matches the prefix replies after a jitter of
48	   `serial[5] mod 24` milliseconds with `OP_HERE` (0x12) carrying its full serial.
49	3. Collisions are detected by CRC failure; the gateway lengthens the prefix by one bit and
50	   repeats. Worst case is 48 rounds.
51	4. Gateway assigns an address with `OP_ADOPT` (0x13), payload = serial (6 bytes) + new `ADDR`
52	   (1 byte). The node writes it to flash and replies `OP_ACK`.
53	
54	A node that receives `OP_ADOPT` while already addressed replies `ERR_ADOPTED` (see §6).
55	
56	## 4. Register model
57	
58	Each node exposes a flat register file. Registers are 16-bit addressed, 1–8 bytes wide, and
59	carry a type tag in their descriptor.
60	
61	| reg | name | width | type | units | notes |
62	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
63	| `0x0100` | `AIR_TEMP` | 2 | int16 | 0.01 °C | −4000..8500 |
64	| `0x0102` | `AIR_RH` | 2 | uint16 | 0.01 % | 0..10000 |
65	| `0x0104` | `CO2_PPM` | 2 | uint16 | ppm | 0..40000, 0xFFFF = over-range |
66	| `0x0106` | `PAR` | 4 | uint32 | µmol·m⁻²·s⁻¹ ×1000 | |
67	| `0x0108` | `LEAF_WET` | 1 | uint8 | 0..100 | derived, not measured |
68	| `0x0110` | `SOIL_VWC_A` | 2 | uint16 | 0.01 % | probe A |
69	| `0x0112` | `SOIL_VWC_B` | 2 | uint16 | 0.01 % | probe B, 0xFFFE = absent |
70	| `0x0114` | `SOIL_EC` | 2 | uint16 | µS/cm | |
71	| `0x0200` | `BATT_MV` | 2 | uint16 | mV | |
72	| `0x0202` | `UPTIME_S` | 4 | uint32 | s | wraps at 2^32 |
73	| `0x0300` | `SAMPLE_MS` | 4 | uint32 | ms | writable, 2000..3600000 |
